item.title: How a Pittsburgh-born umpire painted baseball history onto the ball itself
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-condensed version. This text was produced by an LLM from the original article and may omit details. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Why it is here: Engaging narrative about an unusual aspect of baseball history and the artist's contribution.

George Sosnak, a Pittsburgh-born minor league umpire and self-taught artist, painted over 800 baseballs depicting players, team insignia, and statistics. An exhibit at the Westmoreland Museum showcases over 60 of his works, which often feature juxtaposed moments and legends like Harold Traynor, Bill Mazeroski, and Roberto Clemente. Sosnak's detailed paintings, combining American folk art and the talismanic nature of baseball, create treasured relics from disposable game balls.

item.title: After gutting newsrooms, McClatchy plans to rebuild itself around AI
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-condensed version. This text was produced by an LLM from the original article and may omit details. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source.

Why it is here: Analysis of a media company's strategic shift with relevant context and detail.

McClatchy Media, facing a 17% decline in digital subscribers and 39% drop in unique visitors, plans to rebuild around AI. The company laid off over 90 journalists and is integrating AI into all operations, including new lifestyle websites. CEO Tony Hunter emphasized the need for change due to the evolving marketplace. The rebranding includes four new websites, each powered by AI. The initiative, 'Project Catalyst,' aims to automate tasks and streamline operations. Journalists express concern about the shift away from traditional news.

Source: Nieman Lab | Published: 2026-11-18 17:35 UTC

Original link: https://www.niemanlab.org/2026/11/after-gutting-newsrooms-mcclatchy-plans-to-rebuild-itself-around-ai/
